item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I've just never liked the idea of the CotBG literally being cyborgs.

This is just a natural extension of the ideas presented in SCP-217. The Clockwork Virus is used to turn anything organic into a living clockwork sculpture, which is very painful. Only the truly faithful of the Church of the Broken God would go through it; surgical conversion versus a painful virus. Which would you choose?

Be that as it may, the entire idea just goes way too far beyond the limits of what's currently technologically feasible for my tastes

Firstly: this is science fiction, specifically cyberpunk. Cyberpunk isn't exactly the most scientifically accurate genre when it comes to the limits of mechanical augmentations; just look at Deus Ex, where one of the augmentations in Human Revolution turns you into a literal human bomb.

Secondly, I would like to note that things such as the extra eyes mentioned in this story do exist in some form today, as does Robotic Surgery (which the doctor is essentially the manifestation of). Brain-computer interfaces, such as the WiFi enabled Pineal Gland and enhanced data storage, are admittedly ahead of its time. However, brainwave responsive technology- including things like Toys that you play with using your mind- already exists, and is apparently cheap enough that you can get things like the toy I just mentioned for $60 US.

and I can't imagine how you'd keep the entire world from learning about and wanting this tech.

Who says that they would want to keep it a secret? The Church of the Broken God has only 300,000 members worldwide; that's half the size of Rastafarianism. This means that this specific sect may have about 100,000 members, if they're lucky. So, they may openly advertise things like "Come Reject Flesh and Get Cool Augmentations", only to have organizations like the Foundation or the GOC and even the Horizon Initiative take them down. Maybe this church wants to get all the 'cool kids' to join up with them.

I realize that most of what I said probably won't change your opinion about this, but I hope I can at least change the opinion of a few other readers with these statements.

The one issue I have is the fact that Marcus knows the definition of "luddites".

When you worship Technology, Ned Ludd is like a minor demon; he's probably known as The Smasher of Looms, so calling someone a Luddite would be a legitimate insult.

I wonder what would of happoned to Xbox chick if Microsoft had their "always on DRM". If she lost internet connection would she just explode?

That would be implying that Young Maxwellians don't crack the DRM on all of their implants within a week of getting them. Seriously, I can guarantee that the Xbox Girl is breaching the terms of service in about 20 different ways in her appearance in this tale. All though, it does make playing on the Kinect a pain; gotta remove an eye to get it to work.
